questions.question: Who was Alexander the Great's father?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that Alexander was the son of Philip II.
Incorrect. Darius III was the Persian king whom Alexander overthrew.
Incorrect. Aristotle was Alexander's tutor, not his father.
Incorrect. Bucephalas was Alexander's horse.

questions.question: At what age did Alexander ascend to the throne after Philip was assassinated?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says he ascended to the throne at the age of 20.
Incorrect. 16 was when his education under Aristotle ended and he became regent.
Incorrect. 13 was when Philip began searching for a tutor.
Incorrect. 30 was the age by which he had created one of the largest empires.

questions.question: Who tutored Alexander until the age of 16?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states Alexander was tutored by Aristotle until the age of 16.
Incorrect. Leonidas was a strict tutor during Alexander's childhood, but not until age 16.
Incorrect. Lysimachus of Acarnania tutored Alexander in childhood, but not until age 16.
Incorrect. Plutarch was an ancient biographer who wrote about Alexander, not his tutor.

questions.question: In what year did Alexander launch his pan-Hellenic invasion of the Achaemenid Persian Empire?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states he launched the invasion in 334 BC.
Incorrect. 336 BC was when Alexander became king.
Incorrect. 335 BC was when he launched a campaign in the Balkans.
Incorrect. 326 BC was when he invaded India.

questions.question: In what year did Alexander invade India?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states Alexander invaded India in 326 BC.
Incorrect. 334 BC was when he invaded the Persian Empire.
Incorrect. 323 BC was the year Alexander died.
Incorrect. 336 BC was when Alexander became king.

questions.question: Where did Alexander die?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states Alexander died in Babylon, Mesopotamia.
Incorrect. Pella was Alexander's birthplace.
Incorrect. Athens is not mentioned as his place of death.
Incorrect. Alexandria was a city he founded in Egypt.

questions.question: Which city did Alexander found that is described as the most prominent?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says the most prominent city he founded was Alexandria in Egypt.
Incorrect. Bucephala was named after his horse Bucephalas.
Incorrect. Alexandropolis was founded when Alexander was regent at age 16.
Incorrect. Pella was the capital of Macedon and Alexander's birthplace.

questions.question: Which battle was Alexander's important victory over the Indian king Porus?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states Alexander achieved victory over Porus at the Battle of the Hydaspes.
Incorrect. The Battle of Issus was a decisive battle against the Persians.
Incorrect. The Battle of Gaugamela was a decisive battle against the Persians.
Incorrect. The Battle of Thebes occurred earlier during Alexander's reassertion of control in Greece.

questions.question: What was the name of Alexander's horse?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states Alexander named the horse Bucephalas, meaning 'ox-head'.
Incorrect. Parmenion was one of Philip's generals.
Incorrect. Cleitus the Black was Alexander's future general.
Incorrect. Hephaestion was one of Alexander's companions and future generals.

questions.question: What period conventionally begins with Alexander's death?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states Alexander's death marks the conventional beginning of the Hellenistic period.
Incorrect. The Classical period is not mentioned as beginning with his death.
Incorrect. The Roman Empire came later.
Incorrect. The Byzantine Empire came much later.
